bull.b: Renewed revenue growth alongside a substantially higher average selling price indicates stronger demand for Amazfit’s newer and premium products. This mix shift can improve revenue quality, support brand positioning, and create a more durable foundation for future growth than volume expansion alone.

Gaining value share across the United States, Europe, and Asia Pacific shows that Amazfit is strengthening its competitive position in important markets. The expanding Zepp software ecosystem and training features can reinforce user engagement, differentiation, and retention across devices.

The richer product mix and improved gross margin in Q2 suggest that premium models are becoming a more meaningful part of the business. Combined with more than nine planned 2026 launches, continued product development could support mix improvement and operating leverage over time.

bear.b: Revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable profitability, as the latest quarter still produced a sizeable net loss that widened year over year. Continued losses can constrain reinvestment flexibility and make the company more dependent on successful execution of its turnaround plans.

Negative operating and free cash flow indicate that the business has not reliably funded its operations internally. Combined with leverage slightly above equity, this reduces financial flexibility and leaves less capacity to absorb prolonged losses or fund product investment without balance-sheet support.

Memory-cost inflation creates a structural pressure point for a hardware-led business, while foreign-exchange effects and elevated spending further weigh on margins. Unless pricing, sourcing, and expense controls offset these factors, gross-margin gains may remain difficult to convert into earnings.
